answer_part:
The CONTROL device formulation employs p-MeO-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL as a perovskite precursor additive, which contributes to interfacial recombination losses and suboptimal energy alignment. This para-substituted phenethylammonium chloride derivative features an electron-donating methoxy group that elevates its highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) level relative to the perovskite valence band. Consequently, the energy mismatch creates a small barrier for hole extraction at the perovskite/hole-transport interface, increasing non-radiative recombination and limiting Voc. Additionally, the steric bulk of the para-methoxy group impedes uniform molecular packing during film crystallization, leading to localized pinholes and grain boundary defects that reduce charge carrier mobility and FF. These limitations manifest in the CONTROL device's measured 1.188 V Voc and 80.30% FF, despite a strong Jsc of 26.62 mA/cm².  

Replacing p-MeO-PEACl with m-F-PEACl at an identical concentration of 2.0 mg/mL addresses these failure modes through strategic molecular engineering. The meta-fluoro substitution introduces an electron-withdrawing group that lowers the additive's HOMO level, improving energy alignment with the perovskite valence band and minimizing interfacial energy losses. This reduces voltage-dependent recombination, directly elevating Voc. Simultaneously, the smaller van der Waals radius of fluorine versus methoxy enables denser molecular packing at grain boundaries, suppressing ion migration pathways and passivating undercoordinated lead ions more effectively. The resulting film exhibits fewer shunting paths and enhanced crystallinity, which improves charge extraction efficiency and mitigates FF losses from interfacial traps. Although the fluorine substitution slightly reduces the additive's hydrophobicity, the concentration remains below the threshold for moisture-induced degradation, preserving long-term stability without compromising the Jsc.  

The optimized formulation maintains all other components unchanged: Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅I₃ precursor at 1.65 mol/L, MACl at 15.0 mg/mL, 4,4,4-NA SAM at 0.5 mg/mL, and PDADI passivation at 0.5 mg/mL. This targeted adjustment yields an improved device with Voc in the range of 1.174–1.214 V, Jsc of 26.31–26.71 mA/cm², FF of 81.92–83.92%, and PCE spanning 25.3–27.1%. The Voc gain primarily stems from reduced interfacial recombination, while the FF improvement arises from better film morphology and reduced series resistance. The Jsc remains stable due to preserved bulk optoelectronic properties, confirming that the additive swap specifically targets interfacial and grain boundary defects without altering light-harvesting efficiency.

control_device_fabrication: A PCE of 25.3859% with a VOC of 1.18778 V, a JSC of 26.6164 mA/cm², and an FF of 80.2987% was obtained. The precursor solutions for all Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3 films were prepared by dissolving equimolar concentrations (1.65 mol/L). Incorporating 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) as a SAM was critical to adjust interfacial energy levels and refine the perovskite interface. For the additives treated cells, the MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and p-MeO-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) were added into the perovskite precursor solution. The deposition process involved a two-step spin sequence (1000 rpm/5 s and 5500 rpm/30 s) to achieve a controlled film thickness. According to the antisolvent method, 150 µL of antisolvent was dropped on the film 15 s before the end of the program. The subsequent film was then heated at 110 °C for 15 min to obtain the bright perovskite film. To enhance device performance, PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) was spin-coated onto the sample surface as a passivation layer. The spin-coating process for the passivation layer involved 5000 rpm and 30 s. The passivator volume of 70 µL was dropped at 6 s during spin-coating. The passivation layer was subjected to annealing at 100 °C for 5 min. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
